clue.text: He made cuts and let his clients down most reprehensibly!

definitions.text: He made cuts and let his clients down most reprehensibly!

parts.words: He made cuts and let his clients down most reprehensibly!
parts.note: the cuts are a barber's haircuts and letting clients down is literal: the fictional demon barber of Fleet Street dropped customers through a trapdoor to their deaths

explanation.surface: A complaint about a hairdresser who treated his customers shabbily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' seems to mean disappointed, but the London barber of Victorian melodrama tipped his customers from the chair into the cellar, where they were murdered and baked into pies.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description of the murderous fictional barber, whose trick chair sent shaved customers down to their deaths.

clue.text: Check-up involving a certain ceremony

explanation.surface: A medical examination that turns out to include some ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: A car or boiler gets a routine check-up called this, and a church ritual such as a wedding or funeral is also one.

clue.text: Dodge the first mate admits these days

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the first mate takes the other piece inside herself

parts.note: Eve was the first mate, partner of Adam in Genesis
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: An instruction to sidestep a ship's first mate, who confesses something about modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' suggests a ship's officer, but it is Eve, Adam's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or sidestep it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Never sins-could be due to angst

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of the two words may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Someone who never sins might be acting out of anxiety rather than virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is anxiety or jumpiness, which is what a state of jittery nerves amounts to.

clue.text: An American tug

explanation.surface: A US citizen pulling on something.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yank is informal for a US citizen, and to yank something is to give it a sharp tug.

clue.text: Remain too long because of support given

parts.note: over can mean on account of, as in a row over money
a stay is a prop or support, as in a corset stay

explanation.surface: Someone lingers past their welcome because they have been given backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay a welcome is to linger beyond the proper time.

clue.text: Naiad transformed into a goddess

indicators.note: transformed tells us the letters of the water nymph's name are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A water nymph from myth is changed into a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges NAIAD; Diana is the Roman goddess of the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting and the moon.

clue.text: Prepared to use feathers

parts.note: reads as getting ready to employ quills, but describes a bird smoothing and tidying its plumage with its beak

explanation.surface: Someone getting ready to use quills or a feather duster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird that has groomed its plumage with its beak has tidied itself, making itself ready.

clue.text: Study the way a worker is sustained

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A time-and-motion instruction to observe how a labourer keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sustained' looks like part of the instruction but is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sustained is continuous and unvarying, kept up without a break.

clue.text: Give a new set back and a row results

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: Turning around a stage set provokes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but here it is a line of things.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into a fresh order or layout is to give them a new set.

clue.text: Make up for lunch-time

explanation.surface: Compensating for something at the midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends for a wrong is to atone for it, and read as two words the answer is one o'clock, a usual time for lunch.

clue.text: To be enveloped in a flag would appear a bloomer

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside, so the verb goes within the plant

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, a waterside plant
be is the verb to be

explanation.surface: Wrapping oneself in a national flag might look like a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a gaffe but is a flowering plant; IBERIS is candytuft, a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberis, the candytuft, is a flowering plant, and anything that blooms can be called a bloomer.

clue.text: Criminal, but like the skinhead doubly popular

indicators.note: doubly says the preceding pair of pieces is written out twice

parts.note: as means like
read as skin's head: the first letter of the word skin
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A thug resembling a shaven-headed youth is twice as well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' is not a thug here: it reads as the head of 'skin', the letter S, and 'doubly' writes the like-plus-S pair twice before the popular piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer who kills to order is a criminal of the most serious kind.

clue.text: Where high-fliers choose to bring up their youngsters

definitions.text: Where high-fliers choose to bring up their youngsters

parts.words: Where high-fliers choose to bring up their youngsters
parts.note: high-fliers sound like ambitious executives, but are eagles and other birds of prey raising chicks in lofty nests

explanation.surface: Ambitious professionals pick a place to raise their children.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest, built high on a crag, is where the chicks are reared.

clue.text: Presented, though plastered

explanation.surface: Something handed over even though the giver was drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance or bill can be given or delivered in this way, and a wall coated with plaster or cement has been treated the same.

clue.text: Personal cover has its place here, and that's odd

definitions.text: Personal cover has its place here

indicators.note: odd means peculiar, so the letters of the phrase are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: A remark that it is strange for one's own hat to have a set spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges AND THAT'S; 'Personal cover' is a hat, and the definition is where it is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallway stand with hooks is where a hat, one's personal head covering, is hung.

clue.text: What one may eat at length when all wound up

definitions.text: What one may eat at length when all wound up

parts.words: What one may eat at length when all wound up
parts.note: suggests a stressed person eating a long meal, but describes long strands of pasta twirled round a fork

explanation.surface: A tense person eats a long meal to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin Italian pasta strands are eaten by being twirled around a fork.

clue.text: Concerning stout newsman

parts.note: re means about or concerning
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: A heading about a heavy-set journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for fat, but it is a beer; porter is a dark ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gathers and writes news stories is a newsman.

clue.text: Left at home, detained by one of the family

indicators.note: detained by means held inside, so the home piece sits within the relative

parts.note: a sister is one of the family
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone left at home and kept back by a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb but is the heraldic sense: sinister is Latin for left.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the left-hand side of a shield is called sinister, from Latin.

clue.text: Hustle the slipshod operator

explanation.surface: Hurrying a careless worker along.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry quickly is to hustle, and one who scamps work, doing it carelessly, could be called a scamp-er.

clue.text: Colour over the French turn

parts.note: past means over, as in the danger is past

indicators.note: turn means the French article is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's colour is over, and it is his go.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a soft, pale colour, a shade rather than a hue.

clue.text: Generally well-arranged gallery

indicators.note: well-arranged says the letters of the art room word are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A neatly hung art gallery, on the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Largely and generally both mean for the most part, on the whole.

clue.text: Dislike having to provide a translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering of a text in another language

explanation.surface: Someone resents being made to produce a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong dislike or distaste.

clue.text: Parties given in a ship loaded with fish

indicators.note: loaded with means the ship carries the fish inside it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: Party guests arriving on a vessel full of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parties' suggests celebrations, but means opposing groups in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The two parties in a contest or lawsuit are its opposing teams.

clue.text: Search made for drink

indicators.note: made here signals that a new arrangement is formed out of the letters given

explanation.surface: A hunt is undertaken to find a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken after another, such as a beer after a whisky.

clue.text: A woman from the embassy billets military personnel

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of the two words

explanation.surface: A female from the embassy finds lodgings for soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits in embasSY BILlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybil is a woman's first name, as in Basil Fawlty's wife.

clue.text: A writer to embrace with love

parts.note: to hug is to embrace
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: An author is invited to cuddle affectionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo was the French novelist of Les Misérables.

clue.text: Argue quietly to get ahead

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to be in the lead is to be ahead

explanation.surface: Someone advised to debate softly in order to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead a case is to argue it, as a lawyer does in court.

clue.text: Can be relied upon to have a piece of furniture containing rust

indicators.note: containing means the furniture holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Something dependable despite a corroded table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' splits the furniture word after its first letter to take the corrosion inside; 'a' and 'to have' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dependable deserves trust, so it can be relied upon.

clue.text: A rat or silly eccentric in the matter of dress

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oddball rodent or fool shows unusual taste in clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sartorial means relating to tailoring and clothing, so the adverb means as regards dress.
